issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Animal with two attributes (name: String and age: int) and a constructor Animal(String, int), but the provided solution implements Animal with only a name attribute and a constructor Animal(String). This mismatch between the specified constructor/attributes and the actual implementation (and the template code that expects an Animal type) can confuse students about which attributes to implement and which constructor signature to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification, template, and solution consistent. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to remove the age attribute and specify a single-parameter constructor Animal(String), or (B) update the template and solution to include the age field and a constructor Animal(String, int) plus corresponding getter/setter. Ensure the textual description and UML both reflect the chosen design so students know which attributes and constructor signature to implement.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines Animal with attributes 'name' and 'age' and a constructor Animal(String, int), but both the template usage (Main) and the solution implement Animal and concrete animal constructors with a single String parameter (name) and no age attribute. This mismatch between the specification (two-argument constructor and an 'age' field) and the provided code (one-argument constructors, no 'age') creates confusion about the required Animal API and which constructor students should implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and code consistent: either update the problem statement UML to show Animal(String name) (remove the age attribute and two-arg constructor) or update the template and solution to include an 'age' field and a constructor Animal(String name, int age) (and adjust all concrete animal constructors and example usages like Main accordingly). Prefer aligning the UML with the provided code (single-arg name constructor) unless the 'age' attribute is pedagogically required.
